text:
erin_support: customer reports streaming response truncated — final object missing 

Customer payload: they call our /v1/stream endpoint and get valid JSON fragments but no final chunk and no finish_reason. Client-side logs show connection closed with 200 but stream ended abruptly.

erin_support: repro curl they used:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \ 
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \ 
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-xx' 
```

ana_support: I reproduced locally once — final SSE event never arrives, stream just cuts after last "data:" block without the trailing `

` separator.

mike_infra: can you paste a raw sample of the last bytes?

erin_support: here's the last 2 KB from the client capture (trimmed):
```
data: {"id":"tok","text":"...","status":"partial"}\n\n
data: {"id":"tok","text":"...","status":"partial"}\n\n
data: {"id":"tok","text":"...","status":"partial"}
```
notice there's no empty line after the last data frame, and the final JSON object (the one with finish_reason) is missing.

liz_dev: that looks like the server didn't flush the final event. Could be a code path that writes final JSON to buffered writer but returns before flush on some auth-retry path. Any proxy/nginx in front?

erin_support: customer is behind Cloudflare and using our API key 1-minute rotate plugin — they also reported intermittent 401 then retry.

james_sre: possible sequence: client sends request, token rotates -> server pauses to reauth against KMS -> request context canceled -> handler tries to emit final event but connection closed. We had a similar bug where the finish write was not in the defer path.

mike_infra: deploy-bot shows a recent change in streaming handler a few days ago (commit 9f3ab2) that moved auth refresh earlier. tagging @liz_dev for code review.

deploy-bot: New deploy started: staging/streamer v2026.03.12 (9f3ab2)

liz_dev: I found the code. In stream_handler.go we do:
```
// begin streaming
writeChunk(partial)
if authRefreshNeeded() {
  if !refresh() { return }
}
writeChunk(final) // <-- this may be skipped if refresh returns false after context cancel
flush()
```
we should ensure final write and flush happen in a defer that executes even if refresh fails due to transient 401.

ana_support: customer also reported that setting a client-level reconnect helped surface the missing final object (client did reconnect and received a resumed chunk with last_event_id). but they didn't always get the finish_reason even after resume.

mike_infra: possible two problems: 1) final frame dropped server-side; 2) resume logic isn't re-sending finish_reason when reconstructing response. We should add stronger resume state and idempotent terminal event emission.

erin_support: action items:
- liz to patch server to always emit terminal event in defer and to ensure flush on all code paths (PR queued).
- james to add telemetry counters for "stream_final_emitted" and "stream_closed_before_final" (SRE alert if ratio > 0.1%).
- mike to check proxy (Cloudflare) keepalive and chunked passthrough behavior for 1xx/200 streaming.
- ana to send customer a temporary client-side workaround: reconnect/resume using Last-Event-ID and tolerate missing finish_reason by treating stream close as terminal if last_event had status "partial" for >2s.

liz_dev: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/streamer/pull/458 — core change: move final write into defer, call flush with 5s timeout, and increment telemetry.

james_sre: I'll add the alert and a dashboard tile for final-emitted ratio.

ana_support: customer responded: "we'll try the reconnect workaround and report back; thanks for the quick triage." :thumbsup: 

mike_infra: long term: add test harness that simulates auth rotation mid-stream + proxy timeouts. Also add integration test that the SSE stream always ends with a terminal JSON object with finish_reason set.

erin_support: marking this thread for escalation to P1 if we see more than 3 customers in 24h. ticket: SUP-5289.

liz_dev: patch pushed to canary, monitoring CPU for any regressions. will follow up after 1 hour.

end of thread.
